issues.legal_issue: A person claiming ownership through adverse possession cannot obtain a declaration of ownership by bringing a suit on that basis.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking a declaration that it had become owner through adverse possession.
The trial court found that the plaintiff had been in adverse possession, but denied the declaration; the appellate courts also denied that relief.
issues.conclusion: A declaration that ownership has matured through adverse possession cannot be sought by the person claiming adverse possession as plaintiff; adverse possession is available to that person only as a defence when proceedings are brought against them.
issues.legal_principle: Adverse possession may be used as a shield and not as a sword: a person claiming adverse possession may plead it in defence but cannot use it as the basis for a suit seeking a declaration of ownership. The Court affirmed the principle applied in Gurudwara Sahib Sannauli v. State of Punjab, PLR 756. No statutory provision is identified in the judgment.

predicates.plaintiff_seeks_ownership_declaration: The claimant brings a suit seeking a declaration that the claimant owns the property.
predicates.claim_based_on_adverse_possession: The claimant bases the asserted ownership on having possessed the property adversely.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks an ownership declaration in a suit based on adverse possession, that declaration is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: An injunction decree that was not challenged remains effective, and an appellate court cannot deny its protection in an appeal confined to a different relief.
material_facts: The trial court granted an injunction preventing the respondents from forcibly or unlawfully dispossessing the plaintiff, except according to due process of law.
The respondents did not challenge the injunction decree, and the appeal concerned the denial of a declaration of ownership.
The High Court nevertheless observed that the plaintiff was not entitled to an injunction because it was not the owner.
issues.conclusion: The injunction decree had attained finality, and the High Court’s observations denying entitlement to an injunction were unnecessary and beyond the scope of the appeal. The plaintiff’s possession could not be disturbed except by due process of law.
issues.legal_principle: A part of a decree that was not challenged attained finality; an appellate court should not decide an issue outside the scope of the appeal. The unchallenged injunction protected possession against disturbance except through due process. No statutory provision or earlier case is identified for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_is_limited_to_another_relief: The appeal concerns relief other than the injunction granted by the trial court.
predicates.injunction_decree_was_unappealed: The party against whom the injunction was granted did not challenge that part of the decree.
predicates.possession_was_protected_by_injunction: The trial court restrained disturbance of the claimant’s possession except through due process of law.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns another relief, the injunction was not challenged, and possession was protected by it, possession remains protected except through due process.

issues.legal_issue: In later proceedings seeking possession or ejectment, a person claiming adverse possession may raise it as a defence and may plead that an earlier finding of adverse possession operates as res judicata.
material_facts: The plaintiff had an existing finding that it had been in adverse possession of the property.
The Court contemplated that the respondents might later bring proceedings for possession or ejectment.
issues.conclusion: If proceedings for possession or ejectment are brought, the plaintiff may plead ownership by adverse possession in defence and may plead that the earlier finding on adverse possession operates as res judicata; the Court did not decide whether that finding would in fact be preclusive.
issues.legal_principle: Adverse possession is available as a defence when the claimant is sued. The Court also expressly left the claimant at liberty to plead that the earlier finding on adverse possession operates as res judicata. No statutory provision or earlier case is identified for this clarification.

predicates.possession_or_ejectment_proceeding_is_br: Another party brings proceedings seeking possession of the property or ejectment of the claimant.
predicates.prior_finding_established_adverse_posses: An earlier judgment found that the claimant possessed the property adversely.

issues.definition: If possession or ejectment proceedings are brought against a claimant and an earlier judgment found adverse possession, the claimant may raise that defence and plead that the earlier finding is res judicata.
